# Python and R together

R chunks (```` ```{r} ````) run in R, Python chunks (```` ```{python} ````) in the
embedded Python of Bio7. Both can be mixed in one document. The data are
exchanged with the module `bio7` of the embedded Python:

| Python                        | Description                                  |
|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| `bio7.r("code")`              | evaluates R code, returns the value          |
| `bio7.from_r("name")`         | the value of an R variable                   |
| `bio7.to_r("name", value)`    | assigns a Python value in R                  |

Vectors and matrices become numpy arrays, data frames pandas DataFrames, named
lists dicts (and vice versa). **R must be started** for this example.

## Data in R

```{r}
data(iris)
fit <- lm(Petal.Width ~ Petal.Length, data = iris)
coef(fit)
```

## The data frame of R in Python

```{python}
import bio7
import numpy as np

iris = bio7.from_r("iris")
iris.groupby("Species").mean(numeric_only=True).round(2)
```

## A Python plot of the R data and the R model

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

coef = bio7.r("coef(fit)")
xs = np.linspace(iris["Petal.Length"].min(), iris["Petal.Length"].max(), 50)
for species, group in iris.groupby("Species"):
    plt.scatter(group["Petal.Length"], group["Petal.Width"], s=14, label=species)
plt.plot(xs, coef[0] + coef[1] * xs, color="black", lw=1.5, label="lm (R)")
plt.xlabel("Petal length")
plt.ylabel("Petal width")
plt.legend()
plt.show()
```

## Computed in Python, tested in R

```{python}
# The ratio of the petal width and length per flower (numpy) to R
ratio = (iris["Petal.Width"] / iris["Petal.Length"]).to_numpy()
bio7.to_r("ratio", ratio)
bio7.to_r("species", iris["Species"].astype(str).tolist())
print("Transferred", ratio.size, "values to R")
```

```{r}
species <- factor(species)
tapply(ratio, species, mean)
kruskal.test(ratio ~ species)
boxplot(ratio ~ species, col = c("#66c2a5", "#fc8d62", "#8da0cb"), ylab = "Petal width / length")
```
